hero.headline: US strikes Iran targets for second time in three days
hero.body:
The United States launched a second round of military strikes against Iranian targets within three days, escalating hostilities even as a fragile ceasefire technically remains in place between the two nations. The attacks have triggered severe disruptions to global oil markets and critical Middle Eastern infrastructure.

Oil prices surged dramatically following the strikes. Brent crude, the international benchmark, rallied 9 percent to reach $100.29 per barrel on Thursday before settling back to around $98, still up approximately 6 percent. West Texas Intermediate US crude climbed 8.6 percent to $94.75 a barrel. The price of oil had stood at just $60 a barrel at the start of the year and broke the $100 mark for the first time in four years on Monday, when it spiked as high as $119.

Iran responded with retaliatory strikes targeting economic and energy infrastructure across the region. Several merchant ships were struck in and around the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments. Three crew members aboard the Thai-registered vessel Mayuree Naree were reported trapped following an attack. Iraq halted all operations at its oil ports after attacks on nearby tankers, while Bahrain advised residents to stay indoors following an Iranian strike on fuel tanks. Oman shifted all vessels from its main oil export terminal at Mina Al Fahal after drone strikes at another port.

The escalating conflict has damaged key oil and gas infrastructure across the Middle East. The International Energy Agency warned that the war is expected to cut the region's oil and gas production by at least 10 million barrels per day. The agency ordered the largest release of government reserves in its history on Wednesday, with its 32 member nations unanimously agreeing to release 400 million barrels of emergency crude.

Despite the massive reserve release, the conflict continues to disrupt global energy supplies. The IEA forecasts a global oil output decline of 8 million barrels per day this year, even accounting for increased production from countries including Russia. The agency cut 1 million barrels per day from its global oil demand forecasts due to lower refining and air travel in the Middle East.

Iran's military command escalated rhetoric, warning that oil prices could reach $200 a barrel. A military spokesperson stated: "Get ready for oil to be $200 a barrel, because the oil price depends on regional security, which you have destabilised."

Goldman Sachs raised its forecast for Brent crude in the fourth quarter of 2026 to $71 per barrel, up from $66. The soaring energy costs are expected to weigh on global economic growth, potentially reducing demand further. Asian stock markets came under pressure, with Japan's Nikkei 225 dropping 1.6 percent and South Korea's Kospi index falling 1.2 percent. European natural gas prices rose 7.7 percent for a second consecutive day.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone control station after interception of four drones
cards.teaser: The US military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone.
cards.body:
US Central Command forces intercepted and destroyed four Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz that were targeting a commercial ship. In response, American military assets struck an Iranian ground control station in Bandar Abbas on Iran's southern coast that was preparing to launch a fifth drone.

This marks the second military confrontation between the US and Iran in three days. The strikes occur during ongoing negotiations aimed at ending the three-month conflict, though tensions remain high with both sides maintaining firm positions.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Evacuations in Southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: Israeli military declares areas south of the Zahrani River combat zones and threatens fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel has issued an evacuation order affecting large areas of southern Lebanon, designating regions south of the Zahrani River as combat zones. The military action comes as part of ongoing tensions with Hezbollah.

The Israeli military has threatened the militant group with additional strikes. The evacuation order impacts multiple communities throughout southern Lebanon's affected regions.

cards.headline: Kuwait Reports Missile and Drone Attack
cards.teaser: The attack further challenges the unstable cease-fire in the Iran war.
cards.body:
Kuwait said it faced a missile and drone attack. The incident adds to challenges facing the fragile cease-fire between the United States and Iran.

The attack on Kuwait occurred as tensions continue in the region despite the cease-fire agreement. The strike represents another test of the peace arrangement between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Zelensky urged US officials to supply Ukraine with Patriot missile interceptors, saying Ukraine has not built its own anti-missile defense capability.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. Zelensky urged the weapons systems as a means to help end the ongoing conflict with Russia.

The request comes as Ukraine faces continued Russian attacks on its capital and infrastructure. Kyiv has been conducting long-range strikes against Russian military assets despite the threats of further Russian strikes.

cards.headline: Iranians regain internet access after monthslong shutdown
cards.teaser: Authorities ended a monthslong internet shutdown, though users report slow service and heavy restrictions on apps.
cards.body:
Iranians have begun reconnecting to the internet following authorities' decision to end an extended shutdown. However, the restoration has been gradual, with many users experiencing slow and unreliable connections in various parts of the country.

Major social media platforms and video services including YouTube and Instagram remain heavily restricted. The monthslong outage had significantly limited millions of Iranians' ability to access global communication networks.

hero.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Reach Capital
hero.teaser: Seven confirmed Ebola cases have been reported in Kampala as Uganda moves to contain the outbreak.
hero.body:
Uganda closed its border with Congo as Ebola cases reached the capital. Seven confirmed cases have been reported in Kampala, prompting the government to take preventative action.

The border closure aims to contain the virus's spread from the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo, where the outbreak continues to escalate. Uganda's health officials emphasized that the country maintains robust disease surveillance systems to monitor and respond to potential cases.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Evacuations in Southern Lebanon
cards.teaser: Israeli military declares areas south of the Zahrani River combat zones and threatens fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel has issued an evacuation order affecting large areas of southern Lebanon, designating regions south of the Zahrani River as combat zones. The military action comes as part of ongoing tensions with Hezbollah.

The Israeli military has threatened the militant group with additional strikes. The evacuation order impacts multiple communities throughout southern Lebanon's affected regions.

cards.headline: UN Warns Record Hot Year Almost Certain by 2030
cards.teaser: Global temperatures are set for record highs and could reach 1.9C above pre-industrial levels by 2030.
cards.body:
The world is almost certain to experience a record hot year by 2030, according to a UN warning. A UN weather agency report found that global temperatures are likely to remain at record levels between 2026 and 2030.

Temperatures could hit 1.9C above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The report indicates that global temperatures are set to reach near-record highs over the next five years.

cards.headline: Australia Sues 3M Over Firefighting Foam Contamination
cards.teaser: The government filed a A$2 billion case against the US manufacturer over contamination at defense sites.
cards.body:
Australia is suing 3M, a U.S. multinational manufacturer, over contamination from PFAS chemicals—known as "forever chemicals"—found in firefighting foam used at defense bases across the country. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the legal action, which seeks damages exceeding A$2 billion.

This represents the largest lawsuit ever brought by the Australian government. The case centers on the environmental and health impacts of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances that contaminated defense sites through the use of firefighting foam containing these persistent chemicals.

cards.headline: Australia Charges Woman With Joining Islamic State After Syria Return
cards.teaser: The woman returned from Syria where she had spent years in a camp.
cards.body:
Australia has charged a woman with joining Islamic State after she returned from Syria, where she had spent years in a camp. Recent months have seen multiple groups of women and children who were held in Syrian camps return to Australia.

The charges reflect the government's approach to addressing foreign fighters and their families who are coming back to the country from conflict zones.

cards.headline: Google Employee Charged With Insider Trading Using Internal Data
cards.teaser: The longtime employee allegedly made $1.2 million through bets using company information.
cards.body:
A Google engineer was charged with fraud after allegedly using confidential company information to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The employee made $1.2 million on wagers related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, risking over $2.7 million in total bets.

Federal prosecutors allege the engineer accessed Google's confidential data about search trends before the information became public, giving him an unfair advantage in predicting the outcome of these wagers. The case was filed in New York.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Thought Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady said she was frightened by Joe Biden's debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was "frightened" by her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and worried he might have suffered a stroke during the high-profile event.

The CBS interview, set to air on Sunday, featured the 30-second clip of Jill Biden describing her concerns about her husband's faltering debate performance.

cards.headline: Former CIA official charged with stealing $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: A former senior CIA official with top secret clearance was arrested after hundreds of gold bars were found in his home.
cards.body:
A former senior CIA official with top secret-level clearance has been charged with stealing hundreds of gold bars worth more than $40 million from the federal government. The ex-official allegedly stashed approximately 300 gold bars inside his home.

The FBI arrested the former officer and recovered the stolen gold. Multiple news outlets confirmed the arrest and the discovery. The case marks one of the largest alleged thefts by a former intelligence official in recent years.

cards.headline: Former federal judges ask court to reopen Trump IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A group of former judges is urging a court to investigate a settlement between Trump and the IRS over potential fraud concerns.
cards.body:
Former federal judges have filed a request to reopen a lawsuit involving President Trump and the IRS. They are seeking a court inquiry into a deal Trump negotiated with the tax agency, particularly focusing on a payout fund connected to the settlement.

The former judges argue the case should be reopened so the court can examine the agreement more closely. Their effort aims to have the court probe the details of the deal between Trump and the IRS.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having a stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. In an interview with CBS News set to air Sunday, she revealed that she thought he might have suffered a stroke, saying she had never seen him perform that way before or since.

Biden's remarks offer a personal perspective on the debate, which became a pivotal moment in the 2024 presidential race. Her account provides insight into her immediate reaction as she witnessed his struggles on stage.

cards.headline: Iranians regain internet access after monthslong shutdown
cards.teaser: Authorities ended a monthslong internet shutdown, though users report slow service and heavy restrictions on apps.
cards.body:
Iranians have begun reconnecting to the internet following authorities' decision to end an extended shutdown. However, the restoration has been gradual, with many users experiencing slow and unreliable connections in various parts of the country.

Major social media platforms and video services including YouTube and Instagram remain heavily restricted. The monthslong outage had significantly limited millions of Iranians' ability to access global communication networks.

cards.headline: Becerra opens lead in California governor race
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Becerra ahead of Hilton in the race to replace Governor Newsom.
cards.body:
A poll released by the Public Policy Institute of California shows Becerra has opened a lead in the race for California governor. Politico reported Becerra is ahead of Hilton as candidates compete to replace outgoing Governor Newsom.

The Desert Sun reported the race is shifting rapidly, while CalMatters noted the packed field of candidates. The Washington Post reported that California Democrats appear ambivalent about their choices in the crowded primary contest.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuation of southern Lebanon areas
cards.teaser: The Israeli military declared areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and threatened fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel has issued an evacuation order for large areas of southern Lebanon south of the Zahrani River, designating them as combat zones. The military warned of potential military operations in these regions.

The Israeli military has threatened Hezbollah with additional strikes in the designated areas. The evacuation order directly impacts civilian populations living in the affected zones.

hero.headline: Pork prices in China hit 16-year low
hero.teaser: A key inflation measure dropped to its lowest point since 2010 as consumer spending weakens.
hero.body:
Pork prices in China fell to their lowest level in 16 years, driven by weak consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs. The decline marks a significant shift in a key measure of inflation in the country.

The price drop reflects broader challenges in China's economy. Consumer spending remains subdued while hog production has created excess supply in the market, pushing prices down to levels not seen since 2010.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading on Polymarket
cards.teaser: A longtime Google worker allegedly used internal company data to make $1.2 million on betting platform.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading after he allegedly wagered over $2.7 million on Polymarket bets and profited $1.2 million. The charges stem from accusations that Spagnuolo accessed confidential Google data related to the company's 2025 Year in Search campaign to place bets on the prediction market platform.

Prosecutors allege Spagnuolo knew the outcomes of his wagers before the general public because he had access to Google's confidential search-related information. The case marks one of the first prosecutions involving insider trading through prediction market platforms and misuse of corporate data.

cards.headline: China building factories worldwide, competitors take notice
cards.teaser: Chinese manufacturers are establishing production facilities across multiple countries as trade tensions rise.
cards.body:
China is expanding its manufacturing presence by building factories around the world, prompting concern from competitors. The move comes as China's trade surplus reaches $1.2 trillion, triggering global unease about trade imbalances.

India could benefit from the shift in global manufacturing patterns. A former Chongqing mayor called for action in response to China's record trade surplus, highlighting growing tensions over the country's export dominance.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam contamination
cards.teaser: The government filed its largest lawsuit ever against the US company over chemical pollution at defense sites.
cards.body:
Australia's federal government has launched legal action against US manufacturer 3M, seeking over A$2 billion in damages over contamination from per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) at defence bases. Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the case, which represents the government's largest legal claim ever.

PFAS, commonly known as "forever chemicals," are substances that persist in the environment and human body. 3M produced firefighting foam containing these chemicals that was used at Australian military installations, leading to widespread contamination at defence sites across the country.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone makers
cards.teaser: The government is negotiating financial support for domestic drone manufacturing companies.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is holding discussions about providing funding to US drone companies. The talks represent a push to bolster domestic drone manufacturing capabilities.

The negotiations come as the government seeks to strengthen American competitiveness in the drone industry. No details about funding amounts or specific companies involved have been disclosed.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey investigate FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: State officials are looking into reports that fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup, with a focus on matches at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford. The probe was announced by New York AG Letitia James and New Jersey AG Jennifer Davenport.

The investigation centers on complaints from fans who claim they were misled about seat locations during the ticket sales process. Authorities are also examining whether FIFA's public messaging around tickets contributed to inflated prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: Tipping expectations rise beyond the US
cards.teaser: Service workers in other countries are adopting American-style tipping expectations of 20 percent or more.
cards.body:
Tipping culture is spreading from the United States to other countries, with service workers increasingly expecting gratuities of 20 percent or more. American waiting staff have expressed frustration when receiving tips below that threshold.

The shift represents a change in international service industry norms. Countries that traditionally had different approaches to tipping are seeing pressure to adopt US-style expectations, raising questions about whether the practice has grown excessive.

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over chemical contamination at defense sites
hero.body:
The Australian government has filed a lawsuit against 3M seeking A$2 billion in damages over contamination from firefighting foam at defense sites. The case represents the largest ever legal action brought by the Australian government.

The lawsuit centers on contamination from chemicals known as PFAS, often called forever chemicals because they persist in the environment and human body. These substances were used in firefighting foams at military installations across Australia.

3M, a US manufacturing giant, produced the foam products that contained the chemicals. PFAS compounds have been linked to various health concerns and can contaminate soil and water supplies at sites where the foams were used or stored.

The Australian government is seeking compensation for the cleanup costs and environmental damage at multiple defense sites where the contamination occurred. The chemicals can migrate through soil and groundwater, affecting areas beyond the original application sites.

The scale of the legal action reflects both the extent of the contamination and the significant costs associated with remediation efforts. Defense installations typically used these foams extensively for training exercises and emergency response preparations over many years.

The case joins a growing number of legal actions worldwide against manufacturers of PFAS-containing products. Multiple countries and jurisdictions have moved to restrict or ban the use of these chemicals in firefighting foams due to environmental and health concerns.

3M has faced similar litigation in other countries, including the United States, where the company has settled cases related to PFAS contamination. The company previously announced plans to exit PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025.

The Australian lawsuit seeks to recover funds the government has spent or will spend addressing the contamination at affected sites. Cleanup operations at PFAS-contaminated sites can take years and require specialized techniques to remove or contain the chemicals.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after Polymarket bets
cards.teaser: A Google employee faces charges for placing $2.7 million in wagers on prediction markets related to internal company information.
cards.body:
Federal authorities charged a Google engineer with insider trading for making approximately $1.2 million in profits through bets placed on Polymarket. The engineer wagered over $2.7 million total on outcomes related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, allegedly leveraging insider knowledge from their position at the company.

The case represents only the second known federal prosecution involving insider trading on a prediction market platform. It highlights how corporate employees with access to nonpublic information can exploit emerging betting markets for personal gain.

cards.headline: Google AI systems struggle with basic spelling and word recognition
cards.teaser: Google's artificial intelligence search features have been producing errors in spelling common words including the company's own name.
cards.body:
Google's AI-powered search systems are displaying problems with basic text recognition and spelling. The issues affect the company's ability to process words like disregard, stop, and ignore, as well as spelling Google itself correctly.

The problems have become noticeable enough that users are questioning whether Microsoft's search offerings could gain ground as an alternative. The errors represent a setback for Google's push to integrate AI throughout its search products.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: The Psyche probe took high-resolution photographs of Mars, including views of the south pole, while en route to its asteroid destination.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby on its journey to a distant asteroid. The probe captured detailed images including views of the planet's south pole that scientists described as spectacular and unique.

Psyche is traveling to study a metal-rich asteroid in the outer solar system. The Mars flyby provided an opportunity to test the spacecraft's imaging systems while gathering scientific observations of the red planet.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for R2 SUV
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle manufacturer will begin customer deliveries of its new SUV model next month.
cards.body:
Rivian has set June 9 as the delivery date for its first R2 SUVs to customers. CEO RJ Scaringe has emphasized the significance of the vehicle, calling it potentially the most important product the company has launched.

The R2 marks a crucial expansion for Rivian as the electric vehicle maker moves beyond its initial truck and SUV lineup. With the delivery date now confirmed, the company is moving forward with bringing the new model to market.

cards.headline: Researchers achieve perfect randomness using quantum computing
cards.teaser: Scientists created truly random numbers through entangled quantum chips, a development with potential applications in cryptography and security.
cards.body:
Researchers have demonstrated perfect randomness for the first time using quantum computing systems. The team achieved the result through entangled quantum chips that generate numbers without any underlying pattern or predictability.

The breakthrough has implications for cryptography and data security, where truly random numbers are essential for encryption systems. Previous methods of generating random numbers have relied on processes that are technically predictable given enough information about the initial conditions.

cards.headline: National Trust applies fresh chalk to hillside figure
cards.teaser: Staff and volunteers will add 17 tonnes of chalk to maintain the outline of a prominent landscape feature in the UK.
cards.body:
The National Trust is refreshing one of the UK's most famous chalk figures with 17 tonnes of fresh material. Staff and volunteers will apply the chalk to restore the outline, which has faded due to exposure to rain and weathering.

The maintenance work is essential to preserve the figure's visibility as a notable landscape landmark. Without periodic restoration, the white chalk contrast against the hillside gradually diminishes, threatening its status as a recognizable feature across the countryside.

hero.headline: Crystal Palace win Conference League with victory over Rayo Vallecano
hero.body:
Crystal Palace claimed their first European trophy by defeating Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final in Leipzig. Jean-Philippe Mateta scored the decisive goal in the second half to secure the championship.

The victory represents a remarkable achievement for the London club, particularly given their journey over the past 12 months. Manager Oliver Glasner has now won three trophies during his time at Palace, adding the Conference League to last season's FA Cup and Community Shield. The Austrian manager celebrated on the pitch with a full-length dive before collecting his winners' medal.

This success was especially significant for Steve Parish, the club's chairman who rescued Palace from administration in 2010. Parish watched the final alongside UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin as the club secured European silverware for the first time in their history. The chairman will now oversee Palace's entry into next season's Europa League, a competition they were denied despite winning last year's FA Cup due to alleged breaches of European football's multi-club ownership rules.

For Mateta, the goal held particular significance. His January move to AC Milan fell through after a failed medical, and he remained at Palace to help them achieve this historic success. The forward's instinctive finish came after Adam Wharton's shot was parried by Rayo goalkeeper Augusto Batalla.

Rayo's manager Iñigo Pérez sent substitutes onto the pitch to pressure Palace's defense, but the English club held firm. The Spanish side reached their first final in 102 years of existence and created several chances, particularly in the first half when they dominated possession. Palace, by contrast, were largely unimpressive before the interval. However, they transformed their performance after halftime, with Mateta hitting the woodwork on another occasion and the Rayo goalkeeper making important saves.

The final was attended by around 15,000 Palace supporters who traveled to Germany. Before the match, both sets of fans unveiled large tifos, with Palace's banner referencing their rescue from financial ruin and their recent FA Cup victory.

Glasner paid tribute to the team's spirit following the match, describing the achievement as making history in south London. He insisted he had no regrets about his decision to depart the club despite winning three trophies in 12 months. The manager's tactical adjustments during the second half proved decisive, as Palace shifted from their first-half struggles to control the match and secure the trophy.

The Conference League title marks a significant turning point for a club that had finished 15th in the Premier League. Their path through European competition to becoming continental champions represents an extraordinary transformation under Glasner's leadership.

cards.headline: Senators introduce bipartisan bill to reform college sports
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell proposed legislation targeting college athletics with provisions including salary caps and transfer restrictions.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell announced a bipartisan bill addressing college sports reform. The legislation, called the Protect College Sports bill, includes measures such as a salary cap for athletes and limits on player transfers.

The bill also targets coaching mobility, specifically addressing situations like Lane Kiffin's move to LSU. SEC leaders are discussing backup plans as the legislation moves forward. The proposal represents an effort to break through legislative gridlock on college athletics issues.

cards.headline: Georgia coach suggests SEC may leave NCAA
cards.teaser: Kirby Smart indicated the SEC could break away from the NCAA to establish its own rules and governance structure.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart suggested the SEC might separate from the NCAA. He indicated support for the conference creating and enforcing its own regulations independent of the national governing body.

The comments came amid ongoing debates about College Football Playoff metrics and strength of schedule calculations. Some analysts warn that such a move could threaten the conference's long-term viability. The discussion reflects growing tensions between major conferences and NCAA governance.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey subpoena FIFA over World Cup ticket pricing
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey issued subpoenas to FIFA as part of an investigation into World Cup ticket sales practices.
cards.body:
The attorneys general of New York and New Jersey have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The subpoena focuses on matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The probe centers on complaints from fans who say they were misled about seat locations and claims that FIFA's messaging contributed to inflated ticket prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: SEC leaders criticize College Football Playoff metrics explanation
cards.teaser: SEC officials objected to the College Football Playoff committee's explanation of how it evaluates strength of schedule in team selection.
cards.body:
Leaders from the SEC challenged the College Football Playoff committee's explanation of its selection metrics. The dispute centers on how the committee weighs strength of schedule when choosing teams for the playoff.

The disagreement intensifies ongoing debates about playoff expansion and conference representation. SEC officials argue the committee's approach does not adequately account for the difficulty of their conference schedule.

cards.headline: Dodgers place Enrique Hernández on injured list with oblique tear
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Dodgers returned infielder Enrique Hernández to the injured list after he was diagnosed with a significant oblique tear.
cards.body:
Enrique Hernández was placed back on the injured list by the Dodgers following a diagnosis of a significant left oblique tear. The injury occurred just two games after Hernández returned from a previous stint on the injured list.

The team called up Alex Freeland from Triple-A to fill the roster spot. Hernández had recently been activated for his season debut before the setback. The Dodgers also avoided placing Max Muncy on the injured list in related roster moves.

cards.headline: Lamar Jackson says Ravens coaching changes feel like fresh start
cards.teaser: Baltimore quarterback Lamar Jackson described the team's offseason coaching changes as providing renewed energy heading into the new season.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson characterized the Ravens' coaching changes as a breath of fresh air. The quarterback spoke about the new staff during the team's offseason program.

Jackson declined to discuss contract negotiations but said his commitment to the Ravens remains strong. He stated the team should leave past conversations about fully guaranteed contracts behind. The quarterback emphasized that his feelings toward the organization have not changed despite previous contract disputes.

hero.headline: Olivia Rodrigo responds to criticism over babydoll dress
hero.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed online criticism of her recent choice to wear a babydoll dress, saying the backlash showed how society normalizes pedophilia. The singer said she drew inspiration from musicians Kathleen Hanna and Courtney Love when choosing the outfit.

Rodrigo said people should not be held responsible for others sexualizing them. The criticism centered on accusations that her recent clothing choices both infantilized and sexualized her.

The singer has faced backlash from internet commenters over multiple recent outfits. She said the logic behind the criticism revealed deeper cultural problems around how women and young women are viewed.

Rodrigo pointed to punk and alternative rock icons as her style influences. Hanna fronted the riot grrrl band Bikini Kill in the 1990s, while Love led the alternative rock group Hole during the same era.

The babydoll dress style became associated with 1990s alternative music culture. Both Hanna and Love wore similar styles during their performances and public appearances.

Rodrigo rejected the idea that wearing certain clothing makes someone responsible for how others perceive them. She argued that placing blame on the person wearing clothes rather than on those sexualizing them represents a problematic cultural pattern.

The singer has built her career on writing personal songs about teenage and young adult experiences. She rose to fame with her debut album Sour in 2021, which explored themes of heartbreak and growing up.

This is not the first time Rodrigo has spoken publicly about issues facing young women in the entertainment industry. She has previously discussed pressures around appearance and behavior that female artists face.

cards.headline: Steven Spielberg opposes AI use in creative filmmaking decisions
cards.teaser: The director said he thinks AI can help solve medical issues but should not take over the creative process in Hollywood.
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against artificial intelligence in filmmaking during an appearance on a podcast hosted by Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson. The director said he does not want AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood.

Spielberg said he thinks AI can be useful for finding solutions to medical issues. He drew a line at using AI as the final word on creative decisions in film production.

cards.headline: Student journalist criticizes CBS News while accepting Mike Wallace scholarship
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos said the recent direction of CBS News stains the legacy of Mike Wallace as he accepted the memorial scholarship named for the journalist.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, criticized CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmys. Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the award.

Campos told the audience that the recent direction of CBS News tarnishes the legacy of Mike Wallace, the legendary journalist for whom the scholarship is named. His remarks drew applause from the ceremony attendees.

cards.headline: ABC News wins most awards at News Emmys, World News Tonight takes top prize
cards.teaser: ABC News led the 47th annual News Emmys with eight wins, while National Geographic won seven awards thanks to Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller.
cards.body:
ABC News led the 47th annual News Emmys with eight wins, including the top prize for outstanding live news program. ABC World News Tonight With David Muir won the award for the fourth year in a row.

National Geographic won seven News Emmys thanks to Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. Both ABC News and National Geographic are owned by Disney. The wins marked a strong showing for the Disney family of news properties at the awards ceremony.

cards.headline: Morris Day denies he will perform at Freedom 250 concert despite being listed
cards.teaser: The singer denied what he called rumors about performing at the National Mall concert, even though organizers announced him as a headliner.
cards.body:
Morris Day has denied reports that he and the Time will perform at a Freedom 250 concert scheduled for June 27 on the National Mall in Washington. Despite organizers listing him as a headliner for the event, Day called the announcement rumors and stated he will not be participating.

The Freedom 250 festival is part of celebrations marking the nation's 250th birthday. Other artists set to perform include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Vanilla Ice, Flo Rida, and others set to perform at National Mall concert for 250th birthday
cards.teaser: Performers including Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice are scheduled for the concert celebrating the nation's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, and other performers are set to appear at a concert on the National Mall celebrating the nation's 250th birthday. Morris Day and the Time were listed in the lineup.

Morris Day denied rumors that he would be at the event. The concert is scheduled as part of celebrations marking 250 years since the founding of the United States. The event is taking place on the National Mall in Washington.

cards.headline: The Beaches see streaming spike after song appears in Off Campus scene
cards.teaser: The band's 2023 song Edge of the Earth saw an 888 percent streaming increase after being featured in a scene from the show.
cards.body:
The Beaches went viral again after their song landed in a scene from Off Campus. Their 2023 anthem Edge of the Earth saw an 888 percent spike in streaming.

The song was part of a scene involving characters Hannah and Garrett in the show. The band has experienced viral moments before, and this latest surge in streams follows the pattern of songs gaining popularity after appearing in television shows.

hero.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported the investigation, which focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition she gave as part of her two civil lawsuits against Trump. The probe marks a significant shift in the government's relationship with Carroll, who won substantial judgments against Trump in civil court.

Carroll filed two defamation lawsuits against Trump after he denied her allegations that he sexually assaulted her in a department store dressing room in the 1990s. Trump called her accusations false and suggested she fabricated the story to sell books. Juries in federal court found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation, awarding Carroll millions of dollars in damages.

The Justice Department has not publicly commented on the reported investigation. Federal perjury charges require prosecutors to prove that a witness knowingly made false statements under oath during testimony that was material to the proceeding.

The opening of a criminal investigation into a plaintiff who successfully sued the president raises questions about potential conflicts of interest within the Justice Department. The department has traditionally maintained independence from White House influence in criminal matters, though that wall has been tested throughout various administrations.

Carroll's legal team has not issued a public statement about the reported investigation. The defamation verdicts against Trump came after years of legal battles, during which Carroll testified extensively about her allegations and the impact of Trump's denials on her reputation and career.

The investigation comes at a time when Trump has faced multiple legal challenges, though many have been resolved or dismissed. The former president has consistently denied all of Carroll's allegations and has criticized the civil verdicts as politically motivated.

Prosecutors in the Southern District of New York are reportedly handling the investigation, according to the reports. That office has jurisdiction over federal crimes committed in Manhattan, where Carroll's depositions took place.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone control station after interception of four drones
cards.teaser: The US military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone.
cards.body:
US Central Command forces intercepted and destroyed four Iranian one-way attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz that were targeting a commercial ship. In response, American military assets struck an Iranian ground control station in Bandar Abbas on Iran's southern coast that was preparing to launch a fifth drone.

This marks the second military confrontation between the US and Iran in three days. The strikes occur during ongoing negotiations aimed at ending the three-month conflict, though tensions remain high with both sides maintaining firm positions.

cards.headline: Former judges petition court to review Trump IRS settlement creating $1.776 billion fund
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges asked a court to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS, challenging a settlement that established a fund for people who believe the government wronged them.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges has asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. They argue the Trump administration bypassed proper judicial procedures by negotiating a settlement directly with the president rather than allowing the court to decide the case.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund intended to compensate individuals who claim the government wronged them. The former judges contend this arrangement circumvented standard legal processes and are seeking judicial review of the agreement.

cards.headline: Federal appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A three-judge panel granted Khalil's request to stay free while he takes his case against the Trump administration to the Supreme Court.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel ruled that pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil can remain free while he pursues his case against the Trump administration at the Supreme Court. The 3rd Circuit judges granted his request to stay out of custody during the appeal process.

The three-judge panel included Stephanos Bibas, appointed by President Trump; Arianna Freeman, appointed by former President George W. Bush; and Thomas Hardiman, appointed by former President Joe Biden.

cards.headline: Senate Republican leaders endorse Ken Paxton after contentious Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Majority Leader John Thune endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his primary victory over Senator John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are moving to unite the party after a contentious Texas primary. Ken Paxton defeated Senator John Cornyn in the $130 million race for the Republican nomination. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone and then publicly endorsed him on a radio show.

Republican leadership is signaling to major donors that winning the Texas Senate seat is crucial to maintaining Senate control. The endorsement reflects efforts to move past the divisive primary battle and present a unified front heading into the general election.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to Homeland Security chief's criticism of ICE facility protest
cards.teaser: Kim defended his attendance at a protest outside a migrant detention facility after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized him during a Cabinet meeting.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim of New Jersey responded to criticism from Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin over his participation in a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. Kim said the matter was not about him personally.

Mullin criticized Kim during a Cabinet meeting at the White House, saying the senator had complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest. Kim attended the demonstration outside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility in New Jersey.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: Zelensky urged US officials to supply Ukraine with Patriot missile interceptors, saying Ukraine has not built its own anti-missile defense capability.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to supply Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. Zelensky urged the weapons systems as a means to help end the ongoing conflict with Russia.

The request comes as Ukraine faces continued Russian attacks on its capital and infrastructure. Kyiv has been conducting long-range strikes against Russian military assets despite the threats of further Russian strikes.
